title: High PreToolUse abstain rate is expected noise, not a recall failure, unless conditioned on relevant tool calls
body:
Before treating a high abstain rate as a bug, split the sample: check whether the retrievals that DID return atoms (abstained=0) matched genuinely relevant tool calls (they did, in every case checked), then check what the abstained calls actually were. PreToolUse fires a retrieval attempt on every single tool call (L1), so a session dominated by ad-hoc exploratory bash/read/grep calls with no related stored memory will show 90-100% abstention even with a healthy store and working retrieval -- that is correct behavior (advisory injection should not fire on unrelated calls), not degraded recall. The real diagnostic is the precision/relevance of the non-abstained subset, not the raw abstain percentage across an unfiltered tool-call stream.

Why: Investigated live on 2026-09-19 against the actual production telemetry store (~/.dd-data/supermem-3892c3ad040f/index.sqlite -- found via src/project.js resolveDataBase(), not .dd/data or .dd/local as first assumed). 1008/1029 all-time retrievals abstained (98%), 200/200 of the most recent (100%). Of the 21 all-time non-abstained events, every one checked was a legitimate match: editing .claude-plugin/marketplace.json returned the harness-install-mechanisms memory, grepping topic_key returned the admission-required-fields memory, a telemetry-related git commit returned the anti-memory against writing retrieval telemetry to git. The high rate tracked entirely with a recent run of one-off diagnostic bash/read/grep commands with no matching stored trigger, not with a retrieval defect.

evidence.summary: resolveDataBase() defaults to ~/.dd-data (not .dd/data or .dd/local), and openStore() derives the actual per-project data dir as `${slug}-${identity}` under it

v1.trigger: When investigating a high abstention rate reported by memory_retrieval_events (e.g. 'X abstained out of Y retrievals') as a possible recall/quality problem
